title: Other bands that came to New York and failed; his notes as proof
summary: He lists later New Orleans groups that failed in New York, argues with the interviewer over sources, and says he kept notes as proof.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Creole band, the next band to come to New York City was Lacrosse Harmony Quintet. They opened at the Golden Glades. They stayed with about four weeks. The pianists went with Gellert, Gladys Morley, and Barbara. They never were heard again. This was a white group. I had never known these boys. Then came Con Brown with his reorganized band to New York City, where they tried to arise letters, and the management walked out while they were playing. That night they tried at Healy's and were run out after the first night. Before they finished the first night, Brown's band disbanded and never tried again. Then came Johnny Fisher and his ragtime group. They failed to secure employment and went back to New Orleans. That was in 1917 and 18. Where do you get that information? Is that from a book there? Where did I get that information? That you just read. I happen to be there. I know when you're there. Oh, you made that note, huh? Yeah, yeah. You see? That's your information. Yeah, yeah. Look, you see here? Let's say this nigga band left there 1912, the goddamn liar. Because if you look at the places that I tell you, here's what I'm telling you: read, read what I can't wait when I

tell no lying. And if you don't find them there, don't come back here anymore. Just Brahmi is a damn liar. What I'm telling you is the truth. Well, who are these Lacoste people? Are they from New Orleans? I don't know. But I happen to know they were in the paper. Now,
you know how I know it? I got all

those down in notes. Every man that came there, every band went bad and what they did and what they didn't do. But I should have cut the clippings out. I only made notations of these things on paper. And I printed it down on a piece of paper for future references that in case anything came up, which I didn't expect, which it did. Now I have the proof.
